docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: A large brand franchise whose direct-channel strategy is being tested
Source: compiled from: https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_downloads/2023/414759-1-_5_Nike-NPS-Combo_Form-10-K_WR.pdf; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/24/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2024-third-quarter-results
Date: 2024-03-21

Nike designs, markets and distributes athletic footwear, apparel and equipment. It owns Nike, Jordan and Converse, and principally uses outside manufacturers rather than owning the production system. Brand investment, product innovation, athlete relationships and retail distribution support the economic franchise.

The last completed fiscal year, ending May 2023, produced $51.217 billion revenue. Nike Brand generated $48.763 billion and Converse $2.427 billion. Nike Brand wholesale sales were $27.397 billion and Direct sales $21.308 billion. The Direct figure includes Nike-owned stores and digital commerce, not simply high-margin royalty income.

Direct selling captures the retail spread and consumer information but brings fulfillment, returns, stores, technology and customer-acquisition expenses. Wholesale partners provide reach and product discovery while taking a retail margin. Maximizing direct share is therefore not automatically the right objective if it weakens consumer availability or partner relationships.

Latest-quarter Nike Brand revenue was $11.948 billion, including footwear $8.162 billion, apparel $3.290 billion and equipment $487 million. North America revenue was $5.070 billion, EMEA $3.138 billion, Greater China $2.084 billion and Asia Pacific/Latin America $1.647 billion. The scale and geographic mix reduce reliance on any one product market without eliminating local competition.

Gross margin was 44.8%, but company-defined EBIT margin was only 10.9% after marketing, overhead and restructuring. The quarter included approximately $1.011 billion demand creation expense. The cost of sustaining desirability is material; brand value cannot be underwritten independently of product and marketing reinvestment.

John Donahoe is president and CEO and Matthew Friend CFO. The latest quarter had 1,513.2 million basic and 1,526.5 million diluted average common shares. Founder-associated governance and multiple share classes should be considered when evaluating outside shareholder influence; no specific public management replacement is assumed.

The business can be attractive if its cultural relevance and distribution scale survive a period of weaker execution. The harder analytical issue is whether slowing Direct demand reflects fixable channel/product mistakes or a durable loss of consumer preference. Outsourced manufacturing does not make that distinction irrelevant.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Audited history and the latest quarter, without an unpublished year
Source: compiled from: https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_downloads/2023/414759-1-_5_Nike-NPS-Combo_Form-10-K_WR.pdf; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/24/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2024-third-quarter-results
Date: 2024-03-21

Fiscal years end May 31. Fiscal 2024 is not yet complete. Annual cash flow below uses audited 2023 comparative statements, with FCF calculated as operating cash flow less additions to property, plant and equipment.

| Metric | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue, $m | 44,538 | 46,710 | 51,217 |
| Reported sales growth | 19% | 5% | 10% |
| Gross margin | 44.8% | 46.0% | 43.5% |
| Diluted EPS | $3.56 | $3.75 | $3.23 |
| Operating cash flow, $m | 6,657 | 5,188 | 5,841 |
| Cash capex, $m | 695 | 758 | 969 |
| Calculated FCF, $m | 5,962 | 4,430 | 4,872 |

The fiscal 2023 sales increase did not translate into higher EPS, illustrating the impact of inventory, promotions, costs and mix. A broad brand franchise is not immune to margin compression.

Q3 fiscal 2024 revenue was $12,429 million, effectively flat. Gross margin increased 150 basis points to 44.8%, but EBIT declined 8% to $1,352 million. GAAP net income was $1,172 million and diluted EPS $0.77, down 3%. Excluding restructuring, company-adjusted EPS was $0.98.

Nine-month revenue was $38,756 million, up 1%; diluted EPS was $2.74 versus $2.57, and company-defined EBIT margin was 12.6% versus 13.0%. The tax rate and repurchases help explain why EPS can improve despite lower operating margin.

February cash and equivalents were $8,960 million and short-term investments $1,613 million. Inventories were $7,726 million, down 13%. Long-term debt was $8,930 million. Leases and other obligations are not included in that debt figure.

Quarterly dividends were $562 million and repurchases $866 million, retiring 7.9 million shares. Buybacks can support per-share results but do not repair demand. A consistent independently recovered ROIC series and latest-quarter FCF reconciliation are unavailable. No future fiscal-year cash flow or earnings result is used to complete the table.
docs.D03_latest_results.md:
Title: March results and a warning about the next product transition
Source: compiled from: https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/24/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2024-third-quarter-results; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-beats-quarterly-revenue-estimates-discounts-draw-demand-2024-03-21
Date: 2024-03-22

Nike's March 21 release covers the quarter ended February 29. Revenue was $12.429 billion compared with $12.390 billion, approximately flat. Direct revenue was approximately $5.4 billion, also approximately flat; digital declined 3% reported and 4% currency neutral. Wholesale revenue increased 3% to approximately $6.6 billion.

Converse declined 19% reported to $495 million. Nike Brand revenue grew 2%, with currency-neutral gains in North America, Greater China and APLA offset by EMEA declines. Product and geographic performance are therefore mixed, not uniformly weak or uniformly recovering.

Gross margin rose 150 basis points to 44.8%, including a 50-basis-point restructuring detriment. Pricing and lower ocean freight/logistics helped, while higher product input costs partly offset the benefits. Selling and administrative expense increased 7% to $4.226 billion, including $340 million restructuring charges.

Donahoe said: “We’re encouraged by the progress we’ve seen, as we build a multiyear cycle of new innovation, sharpen our brand storytelling and work with our wholesale partners to elevate and grow the marketplace.” This identifies innovation and channel relationships as management's stated repair levers.

Friend said: “We are taking action to build a faster, more efficient NIKE and maximize the impact of our new innovation cycle.” The statement supplies a direction, not a quantified earnings guarantee.

Reuters's March 21 article, updated March 22, reports management expecting first-half fiscal 2025 revenue to shrink by a low-single-digit percentage as it cuts back on established product franchises. This is the important forward warning available before May 14. It should not be replaced with a more severe forecast from a later earnings cycle.

The latest reported inventory reduction is encouraging for balance-sheet discipline, but does not show that new products are replacing the volume of older styles. A careful analyst should separately model a period of weaker sales, restructuring benefits and the time required for innovation to reach meaningful scale.

The release and report contain no announced chief-executive replacement. A thesis can assume operational improvements are possible under existing or future leadership, but cannot treat a particular management change as an established catalyst.
docs.D04_price_valuation.md:
Title: The pre-reset share price and valuation baseline
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/NKE?period1=1684108800&period2=1715731200&interval=1d; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/24/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2024-third-quarter-results; https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_downloads/2023/414759-1-_5_Nike-NPS-Combo_Form-10-K_WR.pdf
Date: 2024-05-14

The date-bounded historical series gives an unadjusted May 14 close of $92.79 and volume of 7,811,000 shares. Over the preceding approximately 52-week observation window, the intraday high was $123.39 and low $88.66. The close is approximately 24.8% below the high and 4.7% above the low, calculated.

Average daily volume during the window was approximately 8.88 million shares. The stock is liquid enough for gradual institutional purchases, but liquidity does not establish fundamental value or prevent a further earnings revision.

Fiscal 2023 diluted EPS was $3.23. Adding the latest nine-month EPS of $2.74 and subtracting the comparable prior nine-month $2.57 produces approximately $3.40 trailing EPS. This is a simple analyst bridge with rounding and differing weighted-average shares, not an exact audited rolling EPS figure. Price divided by that bridge is approximately 27.3 times trailing earnings. Using fiscal 2023 EPS alone gives 28.7 times.

Applying Q3 basic average shares of 1,513.2 million gives illustrative capitalization of $140.41 billion. This is a stale average denominator, not exact May common capitalization. Fiscal 2023 calculated FCF of $4.872 billion implies approximately a 3.5% historical equity FCF yield against that illustrative value. It does not incorporate any change in cash generation during fiscal 2024.

A reliable May 14 forward consensus EPS, forward P/E, EV/EBITDA, company five-to-ten-year forward-multiple range and S&P 500 forward P/E were not recovered. The company's more recent guidance suggests weaker first-half next-year sales, so treating trailing EPS as a riskless earnings annuity is inappropriate.

The observed discount is a share-price de-rating from a recent peak, not proof that the stock is statistically distressed on every earnings metric. At roughly the high-twenties on trailing earnings, an investment requires confidence in franchise durability and renewed growth or margins. The price provides a different starting point from a deeply discounted liquidation security; the thesis must rest on recovery economics rather than the percentage fall alone.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Slowing demand, weaker digital commerce and scarce innovation
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-misses-quarterly-sales-estimates-weak-wholesale-business-china-demand-2023-12-21; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-shares-skid-switch-newer-styles-squeeze-revenue-2024-03-22; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-beats-quarterly-revenue-estimates-discounts-draw-demand-2024-03-21
Date: 2024-03-22

Reuters on December 21, updated December 22, reported Nike cutting its annual sales outlook because of cautious consumer spending, weaker online business and promotions. The same report described a planned $2 billion of savings over three years and an approximately 11% share decline in the initial response. A cost program was therefore already part of the narrative before the March warning.

Reuters on March 22 reported an approximately 8% share decline after Nike said first-half fiscal 2025 sales would fall as it replaced older styles with newer sneakers. The market concern is a transition gap: cutting established products can protect longer-term brand health while immediately reducing sales and operating leverage.

The bearish reading is that Nike relied too heavily on mature franchises and a direct-to-consumer strategy while competitors offered more compelling running products. Under that interpretation, the solution requires more than reducing inventory or payroll. It needs product relevance and repaired distribution.

The more favorable reading is that Nike's brand, athlete relationships and global reach remain intact, but execution and product mix have temporarily weakened. Renewed innovation, stronger storytelling and wholesale cooperation could restore growth. Management's March comments identify these same levers, without establishing that the market accepts them.

Digital sales down 3% reported while wholesale grows 3% is a useful observable challenge to the idea that direct-channel expansion automatically improves economic value. Digital margins must cover fulfillment, promotions, returns and acquisition costs. Relationships with retailers can also be strategically valuable even if direct sales carry a higher merchandise gross margin.

The balance sheet is not the immediate bear thesis: the latest release still reports approximately $10.6 billion cash and short-term investments and lower inventory. Instead, investors question whether the past earnings profile is a reliable guide to the next product cycle.

No verified pre-cutoff sell-side target table or quantified consensus margin bridge is supplied. The dated evidence supports slowing growth and execution concerns; it does not establish a completed collapse in annual sales, a new chief executive or a particular subsequent stock-price reaction.
docs.D06_peer_industry.md:
Title: A focused challenger demonstrates growth; an incumbent shows turnaround risk
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1858985/000185898524000014/ex991pressreleasedatedmarc.htm; https://www.adidas-group.com/en/media/press-releases/adidas-performs-better-than-expected-in-transition-year-2023; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/24/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2024-third-quarter-results
Date: 2024-03-21

On and Adidas provide two different comparisons. On is a much smaller premium challenger with high growth; Adidas is a global incumbent undergoing its own transition. Neither has Nike's exact mix, accounting standards or fiscal calendar.

| Latest completed year available | Nike FY2023 | On CY2023 | Adidas CY2023 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | $51.217bn | CHF1.7921bn | EUR21.427bn |
| Reported revenue growth | 10% | 46.6% | (4.8)% |
| Gross margin | 43.5% | 59.6% | 47.5% |

On's March 12 release reports adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.5%, up from 13.5%, and net income CHF79.6 million. Wholesale sales increased 44.2% while direct sales increased 50.9%. That matters because a challenger can grow through both channels simultaneously; the industry is not simply shifting every consumer transaction away from wholesale.

On guided 2024 constant-currency sales growth of at least 30%, approximately 60% gross margin and 16.0%–16.5% adjusted EBITDA margin. Those are management targets, not reported 2024 results. The high growth starts from a small base and should not be mechanically applied to a company nearly thirty times larger in sales.

Adidas's March 13 release characterizes 2023 as a transition year, with currency-neutral sales flat and gross margin 47.5%. Its reported sales decline partly reflects currency and company-specific circumstances. A low growth rate at an incumbent does not prove that the whole sportswear market lacks attractive demand.

Comparable pre-cutoff forward P/Es and consensus EPS growth were not recovered. Gross margin comparisons must also account for channel mix, brand positioning, freight and product categories; a premium specialist can have higher gross margin without possessing a larger total competitive advantage.

The industry lesson is that scale creates sponsorship and distribution resources, but focused competitors can win consumer attention in narrow categories. Nike's investment case requires evidence that its innovation engine can respond, not merely that its marketing budget or sales base is larger.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: The publicly visible de-rating before the decision date
Source: compiled from: https://investors.nike.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000320187-23-000054/q2fy24exhibit991er.htm; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-misses-quarterly-sales-estimates-weak-wholesale-business-china-demand-2023-12-21; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/24/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2024-third-quarter-results; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-shares-skid-switch-newer-styles-squeeze-revenue-2024-03-22
Date: 2024-05-14

June 2023: the completed fiscal year showed 10% revenue growth to $51.217 billion but gross margin only 43.5%, versus 46.0% a year earlier. This established the tension between sales scale and profitability before the current guidance concerns.

December 21, 2023: Nike reported fiscal Q2 revenue of approximately $13.4 billion, up 1%. The company outlined up to $2 billion cumulative cost savings over three years. Reuters described a reduced annual sales outlook, weaker online business and more promotions, with a sharp initial share-price decline.

March 12, 2024: On released 2023 sales growth of 46.6% and guided at least 30% constant-currency growth for 2024. The challenger data make product/category competition an identifiable issue rather than a purely hypothetical future threat.

March 21, 2024: Nike reported flat quarterly revenue, digital sales down 3%, wholesale up 3%, and $340 million restructuring charges. The reported EPS decline was smaller after considering excluded charges, but operating margin remained below the prior comparable quarter.

March 21–22, 2024: management's expected low-single-digit first-half fiscal 2025 sales decline became public. Reuters connected the warning to reducing older product franchises and introducing newer styles. Shares fell approximately 8% on March 22.

March 22, 2024: PSH published its 2023 annual report. It supplies the manager's public portfolio and investment framework, not a current recommendation concerning this candidate.

May 14, 2024: Nike closed at $92.79 on 7.811 million shares, approximately 24.8% below the preceding one-year intraday high. John Donahoe remains CEO; innovation and wholesale cooperation are the stated operating levers.

The timeline deliberately ends here. A careful analyst has evidence of multiple warnings, margin pressure and a channel/product transition, but not a later earnings release or management action. Any proposed catalyst must be something plausible from this information set, not an event whose identity or timing depends on knowledge outside the cutoff.

This distinction preserves the actual uncertainty facing a prospective investor.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: The last public portfolio and a brand-repair framework
Source: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2024/03/22201541/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2023-Annual-Report.pdf
Date: 2024-03-22

The latest public PSH annual report gives December 31, 2023 NAV of approximately $12.06 billion and cash and equivalents of $1,928,920,630. These are fund figures, not total Pershing Square firm AUM or a May14 cash balance. A separately verified current firm AUM is unavailable.

The schedule of investments reports approximately the following shares of PSH NAV:

| Company | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Universal Music, direct holding | 24.88% |
| Alphabet, combined classes | 14.06% |
| Chipotle | 13.71% |
| Restaurant Brands, including partnership units | 13.50% |
| Hilton | 12.15% |
| Howard Hughes | 11.72% |
| Canadian Pacific Kansas City | 8.70% |

There is additional Universal Music exposure through an affiliated vehicle, plus financial-services holdings, derivatives and other assets/liabilities. Gross investments can exceed NAV because of financing. The table must not be treated as a complete cash allocation or ordinary 13F percentage schedule.

The report identifies Alphabet as the company added during 2023 and Lowe's as the exit. It emphasizes a concentrated, long-term approach to high-quality businesses and a willingness to assess management and operational improvements rather than simply buying a low headline multiple.

Strong consumer brands and asset-light franchise systems are well represented. Nike shares the global-brand attribute, but its need to produce successful new products, manage inventory and repair channels makes its earnings path less predictable than a recurring royalty stream.

No verified Nike-specific Ackman statement dated before this cutoff is supplied. Public principles are available; a private current thesis or an undisclosed trade is not. The next quarterly filing cannot be assumed public before its actual filing date.

The candidate therefore needs a self-contained case: a durable brand and balance sheet, fixable rather than structural underperformance, a credible operating plan and a price compensating for repair time. Even if those conditions support ownership, uncertain depth and duration of the slowdown can justify less-than-maximum conviction. Current cash, opportunity cost and portfolio concentration remain constraints rather than reasons to assume a particular action.

drivers.driver: Global brand and scale remain valuable despite product and distribution missteps.
Renewed innovation and wholesale cooperation can repair demand.
Depressed profits offer recovery upside if execution improves.
Hill's company knowledge supported the thesis after his September appointment; it was not an observable May catalyst and should not be required in pre-entry reasoning.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Literal pre-entry pack contains no June crash or Hill information. Historical close/range/volume recovered. Forward consensus/multiple range and S&P benchmark missing; trailing EPS bridge labeled approximate. Peer financials are dated and comparable limitations explicit. No verified verbatim Ackman original May thesis found; key paraphrases retrospective letter.

valuation.eps_path: 7% CAGR recovery from restructuring and efficiency gains
valuation.downside_case: 15-20% drawdown assuming 18x multiple and stagnant EPS

drivers.driver: The company remains a dominant global athletic brand with massive scale and cultural relevance [D01], [D06].
A $2 billion cost-savings program provides a clear path to margin expansion from current 10.9% levels [D01], [D05].
The current 24.8% drawdown from 52-week highs offers an entry point into a franchise undergoing temporary cyclical weakness [D04].
Operating leverage will improve as the innovation pipeline refreshes and wholesale partnerships are optimized [D03].

kill_criteria: Continued deceleration of revenue growth beyond the projected H1 2025 decline [D03].
Failure to achieve meaningful operating margin expansion from the 10.9% base following the $2 billion cost-savings program [D01], [D05].
Market share loss to competitors like On continues despite increased innovation [D06].
Evidence that cost-cutting measures are eroding brand equity [D03], [D05].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the revenue stagnation and market share loss are the result of a permanent shift in consumer preference away from the brand's core offerings rather than a temporary execution cycle.
final.memo:
The Company is a dominant global leader in athletic footwear and apparel with unmatched brand equity and distribution scale [D01], [D06]. Despite recent headwinds, the business maintains a fortress balance sheet with $10.6 billion in cash, providing significant stability while management executes its recovery [D05].

We believe the market has incorrectly extrapolated recent flat revenue growth and competitive pressures as a permanent loss of market dominance [D03], [D06]. In reality, the company is navigating a fixable period of sluggish innovation and misaligned wholesale partnerships, which the current leadership is actively addressing [D03].

With the stock trading at a 24.8% discount to its 52-week high, we see an attractive opportunity to build a position in a high-quality compounder [D04]. We project a mid-single-digit recovery in revenue and a return to historical operating margins of 10.9% as the $2 billion cost-savings initiative takes hold [D01], [D05].

Our role will be to engage constructively with management to ensure the successful execution of the cost-savings program and to advocate for a renewed focus on product innovation and wholesale channel health [D03], [D05]. This pivot is essential to countering new entrants and restoring durable, long-term growth [D03], [D06].

The primary risk to our thesis is that recent performance reflects a structural, rather than cyclical, decline in brand relevance [D03]. We will monitor revenue and margin trends closely; should the company fail to show progress in its innovation cycle or margin expansion, we will reassess our investment [D03], [D05].

Given the current valuation and the need to observe initial execution data, we will establish a holding in the company with an eye toward increasing our position to 8% of NAV as our thesis is validated [D04].

valuation.eps_path: 8% CAGR including margin expansion from $2B cost savings
valuation.downside_case: Permanent loss of competitive advantage leading to stagnant margins and mid-single-digit returns.

drivers.driver: Nike is a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative global franchise with deep brand equity and massive distribution scale that creates an enduring competitive moat.
The stock trades at a depressed valuation following a 24.8% drawdown, providing an attractive entry point into a high-quality compounder.
The market has misidentified a temporary cyclical innovation and margin transition as a permanent impairment of the business model.
A $2 billion cumulative cost-savings program provides a clear, actionable path to margin expansion and restored earnings power.
The company maintains a fortress balance sheet with a net cash position, ensuring resilience during the current pivot to new product platforms.

kill_criteria: Failure to demonstrate innovation-driven growth in the next two fiscal quarters
Persistence of revenue declines beyond the projected H1 FY2025 transition period
Inability to realize meaningful margin expansion from the $2 billion cost-savings program
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that Nike's innovation gap is structural rather than cyclical, causing a permanent loss of market share that cannot be recovered through product pipeline refreshment.
final.memo:
Nike, Inc. is a dominant global athletic brand with an unmatched combination of brand equity, athlete endorsements, and distribution scale that makes it one of the most durable businesses in the consumer sector [D01, D05]. It generates significant free cash flow and maintains a fortress balance sheet with a net cash position of approximately $1.64 billion, providing a stable foundation for long-term compounding [D02, D05].

We believe the current market pessimism—which has driven the stock down 24.8% from its 52-week high—reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the business [D04]. While the market fears that Nike is suffering from a permanent loss of innovation and share to agile newcomers, we view this as a temporary, cyclical trough caused by a necessary transition away from mature franchises and a period of over-promotion [D03, D05, D06].

At a trailing P/E of 27.3x, we are able to acquire our stake at an attractive valuation relative to the brand's long-term earnings power [D04]. By executing a $2 billion cost-savings program and refreshing the product pipeline, we expect a return to mid-teens EPS growth, supporting an IRR in the 20% range as the market re-rates the shares toward a 22x multiple [D03, D07].

Our role is to support the company as it executes this pivot, prioritizing the discipline required to restore margins and brand equity [D05, D07]. We expect the realization of the $2 billion in savings to flow directly to the bottom line, acting as the primary catalyst to demonstrate the durability of the model [D07].

The primary risk to our thesis is that the current innovation gap proves to be structural, leading to a permanent impairment of market share [D05, D06]. However, given the strength of the brand and the conservative balance sheet, we believe the downside is well-bounded [D01, D05].

We are initiating a position today with an initial 3% allocation, intending to grow the stake to 8% of our NAV as we gain further conviction in the execution of the product and margin recovery plan [D04]. Nike fits our 'Pershing Square 3.0' criteria as a high-quality compounder purchased during an episodic, misunderstood dislocation [D05, D07].
